name: MonarchDragHandle
title: DragHandle
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas (grip dots), androidx.compose.foundation.focusable, androidx.compose.ui.semantics.CustomAccessibilityAction, androidx.compose.ui.input.key.onKeyEvent; the caller attaches Modifier.draggable, pointerInput or dragAndDropSource
summary: The grip an item is dragged by: a dotted glyph in a 48dp touch target with a spoken name, idle, grabbed and dropped states, and move actions for TalkBack, Switch Access and hardware keyboards.
whenToUse: At the start of each row of a list, or on each card of a board, that the person can reorder.
whenNotToUse: For a list that is not reordered, use no handle. For the handle at the top of a bottom sheet use BottomSheetDefaults.DragHandle.
api: @Composable fun MonarchDragHandle(label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, state: MonarchDragHandleState = MonarchDragHandleState.Idle, axis: MonarchDragHandleAxis = MonarchDragHandleAxis.Vertical, size: MonarchDragHandleSize = MonarchDragHandleSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, onMove: ((MonarchDragHandleDirection) -> Unit)? = null, actionLabels: Map<MonarchDragHandleDirection, String> = emptyMap(), stateLabels: Map<MonarchDragHandleState, String> = emptyMap(), interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)
enum class MonarchDragHandleState { Idle, Grabbed, Dropped }
enum class MonarchDragHandleAxis { Vertical, Horizontal, Both }
enum class MonarchDragHandleDirection { Up, Down, Backward, Forward }

options.name: label
options.description: The TalkBack name, naming the item: "Reorder Design review".

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the handle. Attach the drag gesture here.

options.name: state
options.description: Idle, Grabbed or Dropped. The component that moves items owns it.

options.name: axis
options.description: Vertical, Horizontal or Both. Selects the grip pattern and the move actions.

options.name: size
options.description: Sm: 24dp. Md: 32dp. The touch target is 48dp at both.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the handle offers its actions.

options.name: onMove
options.description: Moves the item one step. Without it the handle offers no actions and is not focusable.

options.name: actionLabels
options.description: Replaces the built-in action names "Move up", "Move down", "Move backward", "Move forward".

options.name: stateLabels
options.description: Replaces the built-in states "Picked up" and "Dropped".

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The source of the focus interactions of the handle.

states.name: grabbed
states.description: Subtle accent fill, strong accent dots and a 1dp accent outline. TalkBack state "Picked up".

states.name: dropped
states.description: Subtle success fill and strong success dots, as a brief confirmation. TalkBack state "Dropped".

states.name: disabled
states.description: Dots in the disabled text color, no actions, exposed as disabled.

appearance: Idle dots use the muted text color; grabbed uses the subtle accent fill, strong accent dots and the accent border; dropped the subtle and strong success colors, in every theme.
platformNotes: On the web the handle is a button with keyboard instructions and aria-pressed. On Android, as on iOS, it is not a button: activating it does nothing, the drag is a gesture the caller attaches, and assistive technology uses named custom actions instead of keyboard instructions. With a hardware keyboard the arrow keys move the item while the handle has focus; left and right follow the reading order. The web's custom icon slot and hover style are not offered. iOS has a hint parameter; Android has no accessibility hint, so it is not offered. The grabbed state uses the colors of the accent tone.
accessibility: The handle is one TalkBack element whose content description is label; the grip is decorative.
With onMove, TalkBack and Switch Access get one custom action per direction of the axis: Move up and Move down, Move backward and Move forward, or all four.
The grabbed and dropped states are the element's state description; an idle handle has none.
The grabbed handle has an outline as well as a color change.
The touch target is 48dp at both sizes, reserved in the layout.
With onMove the handle is focusable and draws the focus ring; the arrow keys move the item, mirrored in right-to-left layouts.
The color change is animated only when animations are on.
edgeCases: The handle does not move anything itself and does not announce the new position; announce it from onMove or from the list.
It installs no gesture. A drag works only when the caller attaches one.
An empty string in actionLabels or stateLabels keeps the built-in text.
The glyph keeps its 16dp size at every font size.

examples.title: States, axes and sizes
examples.template:
Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space4), verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) {
    MonarchDragHandle(
        label = {{handles.0.label}},
        state = MonarchDragHandleState.{{handles.0.state|pascal}},
        axis = MonarchDragHandleAxis.{{handles.0.axis|pascal}},
        size = MonarchDragHandleSize.{{handles.0.size|pascal}},
    )
    MonarchDragHandle(
        label = {{handles.1.label}},
        state = MonarchDragHandleState.{{handles.1.state|pascal}},
        axis = MonarchDragHandleAxis.{{handles.1.axis|pascal}},
        size = MonarchDragHandleSize.{{handles.1.size|pascal}},
    )
    MonarchDragHandle(
        label = {{handles.2.label}},
        state = MonarchDragHandleState.{{handles.2.state|pascal}},
        axis = MonarchDragHandleAxis.{{handles.2.axis|pascal}},
        size = MonarchDragHandleSize.{{handles.2.size|pascal}},
    )
    MonarchDragHandle(
        label = {{handles.3.label}},
        state = MonarchDragHandleState.{{handles.3.state|pascal}},
        axis = MonarchDragHandleAxis.{{handles.3.axis|pascal}},
        size = MonarchDragHandleSize.{{handles.3.size|pascal}},
        enabled = !{{handles.3.disabled}},
    )
    MonarchDragHandle(
        label = {{handles.4.label}},
        state = MonarchDragHandleState.{{handles.4.state|pascal}},
        axis = MonarchDragHandleAxis.{{handles.4.axis|pascal}},
        size = MonarchDragHandleSize.{{handles.4.size|pascal}},
    )
}
examples.code:
Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space4), verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically) {
    MonarchDragHandle(
        label = "Reorder Idle item",
        state = MonarchDragHandleState.Idle,
        axis = MonarchDragHandleAxis.Vertical,
        size = MonarchDragHandleSize.Md,
    )
    MonarchDragHandle(
        label = "Reorder Picked-up item",
        state = MonarchDragHandleState.Grabbed,
        axis = MonarchDragHandleAxis.Vertical,
        size = MonarchDragHandleSize.Md,
    )
    MonarchDragHandle(
        label = "Reorder Dropped item",
        state = MonarchDragHandleState.Dropped,
        axis = MonarchDragHandleAxis.Vertical,
        size = MonarchDragHandleSize.Md,
    )
    MonarchDragHandle(
        label = "Reorder Locked item",
        state = MonarchDragHandleState.Idle,
        axis = MonarchDragHandleAxis.Vertical,
        size = MonarchDragHandleSize.Md,
        enabled = !true,
    )
    MonarchDragHandle(
        label = "Reorder Tile",
        state = MonarchDragHandleState.Idle,
        axis = MonarchDragHandleAxis.Both,
        size = MonarchDragHandleSize.Sm,
    )
}

examples.title: A grabbed card handle in a grid
examples.code:
MonarchDragHandle(
    label = "Move card Launch plan",
    state = MonarchDragHandleState.Grabbed,
    axis = MonarchDragHandleAxis.Both,
    onMove = {},
)
